checks.what: german-empire loss to ukrainian-people-s-republic, May 1918, Kyiv, Kyiv City, Chernihiv, Sumy, Poltava, Kharkiv, Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhzhya and Zhytomyr. The page says 'German forces then recaptured much of the Ukrainian territory under the control of the Bolsheviks, including Kyiv itself' (no date). The Ukrainian State was established on 29 April 1918 as a 'Client state of the German Empire'. Its listed units include the Kiev, Chernigov, Kharkov, Poltava, Volhynia and Yekaterinoslav governorates and the Tavriiska okruha. It ended on 14 December 1918, when the UPR dossier's December rename takes over. The spec has 982 cells, about 248,000 km2, which matches the eight oblasts. A loss moves only German-held cells. The Soviet ledger hands the land to german-empire in March (Kyiv 100 km) and April. Trial: german-empire_1918 snap releases 870 -> 214 cells. At the end of 1918 the UPR is continuous apart from a few cells. 1919 is unchanged except Zaporizhzhya oblast (111 cells): it is now South Russia's at the end of 1919, following the Soviet ledger's own October 1919 loss to south-russia, where the published draft had Soviet Ukraine fill it by keyframe. There is no change at the 1930 anchor.

russian-empire gain, Tuva, April 1914, from republic-of-uryankhay. The page says 'In April 1914 Tannu Uriankhai was formally accepted as a protectorate of Russia' and that its territory 'largely corresponds to the modern-day Tuva Republic'. The spec is admin-1 Tuva: 631 cells, about 159,600 km2. A protectorate drawn as Russian land agrees with the uryankhay dossier, whose successor is russian-empire (Uryankhay Krai), and with the Russian 1915 keyframe. Trial: the 561 Uryankhay cells go to Russia in April and the 70 Russian Tuva cells are no longer released, so Tuva is owned at the end of 1914. russian-empire_1915 now adds 456 cells instead of 1074 and releases 16 instead of 3, about 13 Tuva edge cells outside Cliopatria's 1915 shape. There is no change at the 1930 anchor.

Mosul vilayet: Ninawa, Dahuk, Arbil, Kirkuk and Sulaymaniyah, 335 cells, about 84,700 km2. The Mosul vilayet page confirms the sanjaks of Mosul, Shahrizor (Kirkuk) and Sulaymaniyah, 'today part of Iraq'. The Mesopotamian campaign page has: 'British troops marched unopposed into the city on the 14 November 1918', after the 30 October armistice; 'The ownership of Mosul Province ... became an international issue'. Date and land are supported. As written (occupation_start), 1918-1919 were fixed but other years broke: Ottoman-owned Mosul passed outright to kingdom-of-iraq at its founding in August 1921. That turned the roles of british-colonial-empire's occupation_start of the same month. In a trial of p1920-p1929 the BCE 1922 keyframe then released 748 cells of central and southern Iraq (Baghdad, Basra, Diyala, Wasit, Maysan, Dhi Qar, Anbar and others) to nobody until 1932. A plain gain fails too: the BCE 1918 keyframe (1918-1919) follows Cliopatria, which adds Mosul only in 1920, so the 1918 snap would release it. Fixed by making the event a gain, matching the dossier's own gain of 14 November 1918 for the rest of Iraq, and adding keyframe_overrides/1. Trials of both windows: Mosul is British at the end of 1918 and 1919 (307 cells), and the 1920 BCE snap adds 101 cells instead of 399. The 1930 anchor is identical to the published one for Iraq.
